extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Annals of Statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and electronically submitting a manuscript to the Annals of Statistics (IMS) via the EJMS, including supplemental files, referee suggestions, revision deadlines, and requirements after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission declaration (originality and co-author approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies (a) that the same work has not been published before; (b) that it is not under consideration for publication elsewhere; and (c) that its publication has been approved by all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required declaration made by submitting authors; ensure no prior publication/ simultaneous submission and that all co-authors have approved submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission via EJMS and manuscript preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions to Annals of Statistics must be made electronically through the IMS’s Electronic Journal Management System (EJMS). Your manuscript should be prepared according to the instructions on Preparation of Manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must register (first-time users complete one registration) and upload the manuscript as a PDF via https://www.e-publications.org/ims/submission/; follow the separate Preparation of Manuscripts document for formatting and content conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register once / upload as PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a first time user you must complete the registration, but you only need register once. As a registered user, you will have the ability to upload your manuscript as a PDF file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is a one-time requirement to enable EJMS submission and PDF upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify subject area(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the submission process you will be required to specify the subject area or areas of the paper from a pop-up list which is also available here. This information will expedite the reviewing process of the paper but will only be used within that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do your best to choose the subject area(s) closest to your paper; if unable to do so select 'Other' and state the general subject area in your comments to the Editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Comments to the editor' to suggest referees
rubrics_metrics.description: If desired, you may use the 'Comments to the editor' box to suggest referees who are experts in fields relevant for the submitted paper with the understanding that the editors, along with the associate editors, may or may not choose to utilize the suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not canvass or directly contact the suggested referees about your paper; suggestions are advisory and may be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental files allowed and description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You may also upload supplemental files. These may include: Unpublished or not easily available papers cited in the manuscript; Letters or messages to the Editors too long or technical to be simply typed into the text box on the main submission page; Supporting technical appendices that may be made electronically available on the AOS website if the paper is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each supplemental file, ensure that you fill in the 'brief description' box clearly. Supplemental technical appendices may be posted online if the paper is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions: submission method, deadline, and treatment after delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit revised papers via EJMS. Detailed instructions are included in the email informing you of the editors’ decision on the original paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a revision is not submitted within two years of the decision date, the paper will be automatically withdrawn from the system. A revision submitted after that time will be treated as a new submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for accepted papers (production files and proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your paper reaches final acceptance stage, you will be asked to provide Mattson Publishing Services and the Production Editor with a LaTeX file of the final version. You will also be asked to supply source files for figures along with a PDF file of the full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later in production, the corresponding author will receive email regarding galley proofs with instructions for returning corrections and links to forms required for publication; comply with these instructions and supply required source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for inexperienced authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors are aware of the difficulties that inexperienced authors (particularly those who are not members of well-established departments) may face; see the Guidelines for Associate Editors for further details of our policy on this matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are an inexperienced author, try to find a colleague (senior or peer) to read your paper before submission to ensure clarity and presentation. If this has not been possible or you have residual concerns, indicate this in the 'Comments to the Editor' box when submitting.
